items.task: Read a list of numbers from stdin (space separated) and print the sum and the count, in the alternating-line choka form with a closing couplet.
Read numbers from stdin and print the average as an integer, in the four-line dodoitsu form with a shorter final settlement line.
Read words from stdin and print the total word count in exactly five free-rhythm lines, one breath per line.
Read a log of lines, count how many contain ERROR, and print the count, with a narrative prose body and a final three-line poetic landing.
items.input:
INFO ok
ERROR bad
WARN meh
ERROR worse

items.task: Read numbers from stdin and print their maximum, in the three-line 5-7-5 haiku form with setup, turn, landing.
Read numbers from stdin and print the most frequent number addressed directly to the input, in the three-line 5-7-7 katauta form with a heavy tail.
Read numbers from stdin and print their total in the three-line 5-3-5 lune form with a distinctly short middle line.
Read numbers from stdin and print their total with the ENTIRE program on one physical line (monoku).
Read numbers from stdin, then in linked renga stanzas with visible pivot handoffs (at least three stanzas alternating 3-line and 2-line), print the sum, then the count, then the average.
Read numbers from stdin, and in the sedoka form (two mirrored 5-7-7 stanzas) print the sum in the first stanza and the reverse sum in the second.
Read a number of hours from stdin and, as a senryu (three lines, human subject, humorous landing), print an estimate that doubles when work is not done.
Read numbers from stdin and print the average, but the third long line must deliver a twist: reveal how many numbers are above that average.
Read numbers from stdin, print the mean, then in the final two lines expand it with the range, in the five-line 5-7-5-7-7 tanka form.
Read numbers from stdin and print the peak and the spread, in the five-line kyoka form (5-7-5-7-7) where the final two lines land a comic turn.

Read numbers from stdin and write a two-voice somonka as a SINGLE Python file: two blank-line-separated five-line stanzas, each shaped 5-7-5-7-7, the first voice printing the count and the second voice answering with the sum.
Read numbers from stdin and print the mean and the sum, in the six-line bussokusekika form (5-7-5-7-7-7).
Read numbers from stdin and sing the sum in a four-line imayo song, each line a long rolling breath of 7-5 rhythm.
Read numbers from stdin, and in the four-line kanshi form (two 7-7 couplets) print the sum and the count in the first couplet, turn and resolve in the second.
Read numbers from stdin and print their maximum in the three-line zappai form (roughly 5-7-5, no kigo required).
Read numbers from stdin and print the range and the count, in the five-line waka form (5-7-5-7-7).
Read a line of text from stdin and, in linked renshi stages (at least three visible stages of two to three lines), print the token count of the text.
Read numbers from stdin and report the sum in a fourteen-line sonnet (three quatrains and a couplet, each line about ten tokens).
Read lines from stdin and report the total lines and the error lines in a nineteen-line villanelle with two repeating refrains.
Read words from stdin and print the word count in the five-line cinquain form (2-4-6-8-2 pyramid).
Read positive and negative numbers from stdin and print the count of positive and negative numbers in the four-line ryuka form (8-8-8-6).
Read numbers from stdin and print their sum in a fibonacci poem whose line counts grow by the golden sequence (six to eight lines).
Read numbers from stdin and print their sum, in the five-line limerick form (8-8-5-5-8) with a comic punchline in the final line.
Read words from stdin and print the token count in a ten-line etheree whose lines climb from one to ten tokens.
